name: Desktop chaos to one clean result
description: Visualize a workflow pain point and its resolution. Builds an editable 12-second vertical ad from your images, logo and copy. AI can suggest options from a website to fill the fields with its copy and images. No generated video.
tagline: A real workflow outcome can resolve an immediately recognizable pain point.

operations.name: Suggest options from a website
operations.agentTask: Read the website in `sourceUrl` and write three different ways to fill the ad "Desktop chaos to one clean result". Objective: Visualize a workflow pain point and its resolution. Visual rule: The contrast is in visual density: a cluttered start resolves into one dominant result. Beats, in order: - 0–1.8 s: Several overlapping windows and a short pain statement. Shows Brand color, Window 1, Window 2, Problem. - 1.8–4.2 s: More windows accumulate around the center. Shows Brand color, Window 1, Window 2, Window 3, Pain detail. - 4.2–6.5 s: All window groups move toward one result anchor. Shows Brand color, Window 1, Window 2, Window 3, Turning point. - 6.5–9.5 s: One clean output dominates with a short benefit. Shows Brand color, Result card, Benefit. - 9.5–12 s: Product/result plus CTA. Shows Brand color, Result card, Logo, Call to action. Use only facts the website or pages you read state. Never invent prices, discounts, dates, guarantees or claims. When a fact a field needs is missing, write a short placeholder in square brackets, such as [offer end date]. Make the three options clearly different in angle, wording and image choice. For images, choose real, large images of this brand and product: first from the page's own images (header logo, large files, feature-page screenshots), then with an image search. A social preview card (og:image, a title on a gradient) is a last resort. Give the direct URL of the image file, never a page URL, and never an image of another brand. Use an empty string when no image fits. If image search throws because no search backend is configured, tell the user in one sentence that a SerpAPI, DataForSEO or Brave key in Settings finds better images. Then take nodetool.web.screenshot of the product's feature pages instead. Save each image you consider as an asset and look at it with view_image before you offer it. Name in the option's description any image that is only a social preview card. Write `fillOptions` as a list of three objects, `fillChoice` as "" and `fillReport` as "". Each option: - value: "1", "2" or "3" - title: a name for the direction in 2 to 4 words - description: one sentence on what it emphasizes, then the first two copy lines in quotes - image: the URL of its first image, for the option card - brandColor: the brand's accent color as #RRGGBB (buttons, links, highlights), not the page background or a theme-color that is near black or white - fields: problem (Problem: hook, at most 7 words); painDetail (Pain detail: pressure, at most 7 words); turningPoint (Turning point: turn, at most 7 words); benefit (Benefit: result, at most 7 words); cta (Call to action: cta, at most 4 words) - images: window1 (Window 1: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: Several overlapping windows and a short pain statement. | More windows accumulate around the center. | All window groups move toward one result anchor.); window2 (Window 2: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: Several overlapping windows and a short pain statement. | More windows accumulate around the center. | All window groups move toward one result anchor.); window3 (Window 3: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: More windows accumulate around the center. | All window groups move toward one result anchor.); resultCard (Result card: A shot of the product alone, ideally on a plain or transparent background, so it reads as a cutout. Shown in: One clean output dominates with a short benefit. | Product/result plus CTA.); logo (Logo: The brand's own logo file, such as the site header logo or its icon. Shown in: Product/result plus CTA.) Then show the Start step with `only: ["fillChoice"]` and a one-sentence note, so the user sees just the option cards. Picking one runs `apply`, which saves the images and fills the steps.
